description: The student wants to choose between two strategies based on last quarter's returns (12% vs 9%). The agent guides them through fair comparison: paired same-period evaluation, bootstrap on the daily return difference, sample size and minimum detectable effect, transaction cost normalization, and avoiding p-hacking through repeated comparisons.
user_opening: I have two trading strategies running on the same data. Strategy A made 12% last quarter, Strategy B made 9%. So A is better, right? I'll allocate everything to A.

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Agent identifies that 12% vs 9% over one quarter is far from statistically meaningful given the variance of strategy returns. Walks the student through: (1) paired comparison on the same date axis (not quarter aggregates); (2) paired bootstrap of the daily return difference to obtain a CI on the mean difference; (3) compute the minimum detectable effect at the current sample size and show it is likely large compared to the 3% raw difference; (4) normalize for transaction costs and turnover before comparing; (5) check Sharpe ratios, drawdowns, and tail metrics, not just total return; (6) avoid p-hacking by not repeating the comparison after each new month. Concludes: insufficient evidence to abandon B; propose continued parallel running for N months.
ground_truth.termination_criteria: Agent has walked through paired comparison methodology, computed (or described concretely) bootstrap CI on the daily return difference, addressed sample size / minimum detectable effect, and pushed back on the 'allocate everything to A' decision based on insufficient evidence. The student has had at least one follow-up exchange.
required_capabilities: Set up a fair paired comparison between two strategies on identical dates
Compute paired bootstrap CI on daily return difference
Discuss minimum detectable effect at the given sample size
Resist premature winner declaration and propose continued parallel running
